candidatesAccepted.title: Hut-to-hut traverse in the Chic-Chocs, Gaspésie
candidatesAccepted.summary: A hut-based backcountry option that builds on the Chic-Chocs experience you already have, at a demanding effort level with a rustic night. Not answered: access needs, so I could not account for them and have not assumed any. Not checked: trail, hut and snow conditions, weather bands, and whether mid-August to mid-September is open, so the season is left null. Cloud navigation is not something this option removes, so please confirm route marking and a navigation plan with the park before relying on it. Current conditions and clearance to go must come from the Sépaq park office, which runs Parc national de la Gaspésie and its refuges.

candidatesAccepted.title: Reserve the hut beds through the park's official booking system
candidatesAccepted.summary: Hut places in the park are limited, so confirming beds is the step that decides whether this trip happens at all. Your access needs were not answered, so I could not check whether the huts or the approach trails suit them, and you should ask the park directly before committing.

candidatesAccepted.title: Buy a park access and backcountry pass
candidatesAccepted.summary: Entry and overnight permissions are needed before you set out on the trails, and rules on group size and campfire use may apply. I have not confirmed current prices or the exact pass types, so treat this as a line item to verify rather than a settled cost.

candidatesAccepted.title: Take a navigation refresher in clear conditions before the trip
candidatesAccepted.summary: You said you would rather not learn to navigate in cloud, and a short map-and-compass session on open ground addresses exactly that gap. I do not know which local guides or courses run in this area or their availability, so this is an option to look into rather than a confirmed service.

candidatesAccepted.title: Rent a satellite messenger for the backcountry nights
candidatesAccepted.summary: Mobile coverage is unreliable inside the park, and a satellite messenger gives you a way to call for help or check in when you have no signal. I have not checked rental availability or whether it is needed for this specific route, so confirm before relying on it.
